slides.title: IDIOM MEANING EXAMPLE GIVE SOMETHING A SHOT To have a try at something. I have never eaten sushi, but I will give it a shot. HAVE A BONE TO PICK An unpleasant issue or grievance that need discussion. I have a bone to pick with you about that email. GO FOR BROKE To risk everything and go for an all out effort. If you decide to go for broke, you can’t be thinking about what will happen if you fail. MAKE A CLEAN SWEEP To remove all unwanted people or things in order to start afresh. The new leaders wanted to make a clean sweep of the discredited old order GIVE THE NOD To show one's approval of someone or something. I gave Amanda the nod because she is the most qualified candidate. HAVE AN AXE TO GRIND To have a private reason for doing or being involved in something. He has no political axe to grind. GO-TO GUY/GAL The person is frequently asked for help in that topic. Amanda’s our go-to gal for computer issues. MAKE A KILLING To earn a lot of money in a short time and with little effort. They made a killing with the sale of their London house.

slides.title: VERBS EXAMPLES INTENDED MEANING HAVE Let’s have a cold drink! Let’s drink something cold! TAKE She took a hot shower. She showered with hot water. MAKE Hello, I'd like to make an appointment to see the doctor. Hello, I’d like to set a date to see the doctor. GO Mum's out. She's gone shopping. Mum's out. She’s still shopping. DO She’ll do my messy hair for the party. She’ll fix my messy hair for the party. GIVE Give me a shout when you are ready. Let me know when you are ready.

Delexical verbs are common verbs that when used with particular nouns have very little meaning of their own.

slides.title: To Consider 1. Have– used to talk about food, drink, washing, resting talking. 2. Take – Used to talk about washing, resting, decisions, problems, care. 3. Make –Used with sounds, talking, plans. 4. Go - Used with verbs to do with moving. Also, with nouns that do not have an ing form, we use the structure ‘go for a’ 5. Do - Used with nouns in ing that have to do with work. Additionally, with nouns when it is obvious what the action is. 6. Give - Used with noises, facial expressions, hittings, affectionate actions, talking. 7. Adjectives are used to add extra information to the action we want to express.

Functions Examples Extend meaning through common word actions I need to go for a walk. She gave me a huge smile. We will have a light dinner tonight.

To consider In most cases, there is a verb that has a meaning similar or equal to the delexical structure. These structures are very common in English and an understanding of them will enrich the fluency of the language.

Work-life balance I work for a global IT company, but because their headquarters is in the States, I do all my work online from home. That means that I don't waste time commuting or making idle chit-chat with colleagues. I work on a project basis, and this flexibility is very valuable to me because it means that I can easily take some time off when my children need me to go to their school performances, or if I need to make an appointment with the dentist. The downside is that without clear office hours, I tend to work well into the evening, sometimes without having dinner to finish a task. It can also get quite lonely working on my own, and I sometimes miss sharing ideas with colleagues. Adapted from https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/skills/reading/upper-intermediate-b2/work-life-balance
